title: A phase gate that says where it came from and what it cost
desiredOutcome: A new phase's gate lists meta.phaseGate.always first and drops no buildCommands key unless meta.phaseGate.exclude names it, with that exclusion printed by add-phase, the validator and the sign-off run alike (and 'phase gate runs no suite' when nothing suite-running is left); a gate-only task left with no test file gets the always entries; retarget --gate-drop and --gate-set change a phase's gate in one validated write; the SAME SUITE line, the doctor's economy row and a fix task opened from a red sign-off run each name the next command; and an executor's own tests run through run-test-gate.py --own --quiet with the whole output in a local log file.

tasks.title: The test-shaped predicate and the gate-path reader live beside tests_add_path
tasks.description: Constraint: 'is this path a test file' is answered in run-test-gate.py (_TEST_MARKS, _TEST_DIRS, _subject_of, _segments, _is_suite_path) and 'which paths does a gate entry name' in audit-task.py (_gate_entry_paths). Both files are entry points and an entry point cannot import another, so the gate-only narrowing (audit-task) and --own (run-test-gate) could only reach them by copying. Rule: MOVE them, bodies and docstrings unchanged, into plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_manifest_phases.py beside tests_add_path (the file-naming question both build on) as public TEST_MARKS, TEST_DIRS, subject_of, path_segments, is_suite_path, gate_entry_paths. run-test-gate.py and audit-task.py import _manifest_phases and keep thin module aliases (_is_suite_path = _phases.is_suite_path, and so on) so every caller and every existing case keeps its name: an alias, never a second body. Not _manifest_vocab: its docstring says it holds no rule, and _task_outputs was moved out of it because a path rule is not vocabulary. One widening, classification only: is_suite_path also answers True for a basename starting with test_ (pytest's prefix form, which the plan gate's default exemptGlobs already treats as a test file via **/test_*.*); subject_of stays suffix-only, because it re-spells a path onto another file's stem and the prefix must not start doing that. The widening also reaches run-test-gate's suite_paths and evidence_paths classification, in the same direction; run the whole of test_run_test_gate.py and read any case that moved. Reuse: tests_add_path (_manifest_phases.py), the moved bodies as they are. Red-first: test__manifest_phases.py asserts is_suite_path('pkg/test_orders.py') is True; mutation that must turn it red: drop the prefix clause; allow cases: subject_of('pkg/test_orders.py') stays None and is_suite_path('src/testing.py') stays False. Identity pins in test_run_test_gate.py and test_audit_task.py assert each alias IS the _manifest_phases function (the is operator), so a re-pasted copy goes red. House: stdlib only, no typing/annotations/walrus/f-strings, %-formatting, Python 3.8, cases in plugins/audit/tests/, no register ids in comments.

tasks.title: meta.phaseGate.always/exclude and meta.gateBudgetMs; the one phase-gate default and the one 'runs no suite' rule
tasks.description: The rule this phase holds: no state of a plan may make the sign-off gate run fewer suites than today unless the plan DECLARES it and the gate PRINTS it. Constraint: COMPATIBILITY.md lets a key be added for free only while its absence keeps today's behaviour, and _help.schema_vocab_drift() checks KNOWN_META against the schema, so a key exists in the schema first. Schema, under $defs.meta.properties: phaseGate (object, additionalProperties permissive) with always (non-blank strings meant to be buildCommands keys; they come FIRST in a new phase's default and nothing is dropped because of them) and exclude (buildCommands keys; the ONLY declared way to keep a key out of the default - a coverage key that re-runs the test suite, or an e2e key that belongs at the third place); gateBudgetMs (positive integer, advisory; absent = nothing is graded on cost). Each description says what absence means: no phaseGate = today's default, every buildCommands key in buildCommands order, byte-identical; no exclude = nothing dropped. KNOWN_META += phaseGate, gateBudgetMs. ONE ANSWER FOR THE DEFAULT, used by add-phase now and by the derivation in the next phase: phase_gate_default(meta) in _manifest_phases.py returns {entries, always, rest, excluded, basis}: entries = always in declared order, then every other buildCommands key in buildCommands order, minus exclude. An entry named in both lists stays (always is always) and draws a warning. ONE RULE FOR 'phase gate runs no suite': phase_gate_suite_gap(manifest, suite_keys=None) in the same module, evaluated only when exclude is non-empty (without exclude the default is today's set). A default EMPTY after exclusion returns 'phase gate runs no suite: meta.phaseGate.exclude removes every meta.buildCommands key and meta.phaseGate.always adds none', which needs no evidence. With suite_keys ({running, silent, unknown}, computed from the ledger by L1.e) and no default key in running, it returns 'phase gate runs no suite as far as the ledger shows: <keys> are left after meta.phaseGate.exclude', naming the keys with no recorded run or only pre-field runs as not established. Otherwise it returns None. WHICH PREDICATE DECIDES 'suite-running': the counts reader - run-test-gate.summary_reader (P70 run-test-gate.py:550), the one function that recognises a test runner's own summary line - recorded per step as suiteReader by L1.e. It can only answer from a run's output, so its answer is read back from the ledger rather than guessed from the plan. Not the test-shaped predicate: it classifies paths, and a wide key such as 'npm test' names none. Not the key's spelling: orchestrator.md forbids inferring a test run from a command's spelling. Not steps[].measured: ran_count also tallies a wrapper's hook lines (_STEP_WORDS, pre-commit), so a pre-commit lint reads as measured checks. _manifest_rules._check_meta calls phase_gate_suite_gap(manifest) with no evidence, so the pure validator emits the certain arm only. GATE_BASIS += gate-only-no-suite and failing-from-run (written failing-from-run:<runId>; a reader compares the word before the colon and looks the runId up, never parses it - the schema calls a runId opaque); GATE_BASIS_ANSWERED += gate-only-no-suite; extend the tests.gateBasis description with both words. Other validator WARNINGS, never findings (Validation stays additive): phaseGate not an object; always or exclude not a list of non-blank strings; an always or exclude entry that is not a buildCommands key (name it and the keys); a comma-joined entry (reuse P70's _manifest_phases._comma_joined_gate, never a second copy of that rule); an entry in both lists; gateBudgetMs not a positive integer, or a bool (the budgetUSD rule). SCHEMA_EXEMPTIONS rows in gen-demo-manifest.py for the new fields, with the reason (no rendered surface shows them yet). Red-first in test__manifest_phases.py: always [lint] over buildCommands {test, lint, coverage} gives [lint, test, coverage] (mutation: return always alone -> red); exclude naming every key with no always gives [] and phase_gate_suite_gap returns the certain sentence (mutation: skip the empty check -> red); no phaseGate gives every key in buildCommands order (mutation: sort the keys -> red). In test_validate_manifest.py: exclude-to-nothing warns 'phase gate runs no suite'; always ['lint', 'nope'] warns naming nope; gateBudgetMs true warns. Allow cases: a manifest with no phaseGate gains no new warning; always [lint] alone validates clean, because a reordering is not a narrowing.

tasks.title: A new phase's gate is always first, then every other key, minus exclude; a gate-only task with no test file left gets the always entries
tasks.description: Derivations in plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py. (1) _phase_gate(args, assembled): after --gate-clear and --gate, the default is _manifest_phases.phase_gate_default(meta)['entries']: meta.phaseGate.always first, then every other buildCommands key in buildCommands order, minus meta.phaseGate.exclude. So always is an ORDER and never a narrowing, and exclude is the only declared way to drop a key. The basis comes from the same call: no phaseGate -> today's 'from meta.buildCommands' exactly, with the same entries in the same order; always only -> 'from meta.buildCommands, meta.phaseGate.always first'; with exclude -> '...; excluded by meta.phaseGate.exclude: <keys> - declared out of this phase's gate, and the sign-off run prints it too'; an empty result -> the empty-gate basis naming meta.phaseGate.exclude as its cause, with the validator's 'phase gate runs no suite' warning printed among the post-write warnings. (2) _task_gate(args, phase, assembled, add_paths, files), for a task whose tests.mode is gate-only ONLY: the files arm points the sibling spelling (_path_scoped_sibling + _repointed) only at the files _manifest_phases.is_suite_path accepts. When none is left, the gate is the always entries: meta.phaseGate.always when declared, else the sibling entries _repointed already copies through unchanged (shared buildCommands keys and entries naming no path), in their order; source word gate-only-no-suite and a sentence naming which of the two it took. Never the phase's wide testGate: that is the wide gate per attempt the validator already warns about. When that list is empty too the gate is empty and _empty_task_gate_note is what prints. tdd and regression tasks keep today's files arm, and --gate / --gate-clear still answer first. Reuse _path_scoped_sibling, _repointed, _empty_task_gate_note, _manifest_phases.is_suite_path; value and basis still come out of one derivation (_build_phase's rule). Red-first (dg18): a gate-only task in a phase whose sibling gate is 'vitest run src/a.test.ts', with files src/Button.tsx and README.md and meta.phaseGate.always [lint, typecheck], gets ['lint', 'typecheck'] and tests.gateBasis gate-only-no-suite. Allow cases: the same task with src/Button.test.tsx among its files narrows to 'vitest run src/Button.test.tsx' with basis files; a regression task with only src/Button.tsx keeps today's gate; gb1/gb2 stay green. Red-first for (1), one case per arm. ALWAYS-ONLY: always [lint] over {test, lint, coverage} writes [lint, test, coverage] (mutation: write always alone -> red, because test and coverage vanish). EXCLUDE-TO-NOTHING: exclude naming every key and no always writes [], with a basis naming meta.phaseGate.exclude and the 'phase gate runs no suite' warning printed (mutation: ignore exclude -> red, because the gate is not empty). ABSENT phaseGate = TODAY: the written gate and basis equal what the code this phase starts from writes for the same plan, captured as a fixture (mutation: build the default from sorted keys -> red, because today's order is buildCommands order). House rules as in the repo.

tasks.title: retarget --gate-drop and --gate-set, one write each
tasks.description: audit-task.py retarget <phaseId> gains --gate-drop <entry> (repeatable, argparse append) and --gate-set <entry> [<entry> ...] (nargs='*', so an empty set reaches this verb's own refusal rather than argparse's usage error). Both go through _locked_retarget: one lock, one revalidate-or-roll-back, one phase.retarget row through _journal_retarget with the same changes shape. --gate-drop: every named entry must be in the phase's testGate (refuse exit 2 naming the missing entry and the gate as it stands); a drop that would leave the gate empty is refused exit 2 with 'an empty gate is --gate-clear, which says so'. --gate-set: replaces the gate; empty or all-blank refused exit 2 with the same sentence (dg11). FACT TO FIX ALONG THE WAY: retarget's existing --gate already REPLACES the gate (_locked_retarget: now = [] if args.gate_clear else list(args.gate)) while commands/phase.md says '--gate appends' and commands/task.md says 'That verb *appends* to testGate'; measured on a scratch plan, retarget P2 --gate typecheck turned ['lint', 'test'] into ['typecheck']. So --gate-set is the multi-value spelling of the replace --gate already performs: resolve both into the same now list through one helper, give an all-blank --gate the same empty refusal, and correct both documents to say replaces. _gate_contradiction(args) refuses any two of --gate, --gate-set, --gate-clear, --gate-drop together, asked in the same position every verb asks it. Add gate_drop and gate_set to VERB_FLAGS['retarget'] (the vf group grades the table against the dispatch), to build_parser, to commands/phase.md's argument-hint and retarget section, and to the /audit:phase row of the plugin README (_refs.command_flag_drift fails a hinted flag the row omits). tasks.title: A step records which counts reader recognised it, and a failing step records the suite files its runner named
tasks.description: Constraint: a red row's steps[].failing holds CHECK NAMES, not suite files: for jest an assertion failure is stored as its bullet title alone (_jest_failure_name returns title), so the suite path is dropped. The failed-first fix-task gate, the derived gate's last-failed arm, the shadow recall and the selection-miss pass all need the failing SUITE files. Rule: a reader failing_suites(text) in run-test-gate.py returns (paths, basis): jest -> the paths on FAIL <path> headers (_JEST_SUITE_HEADER, FAIL only, ANSI stripped as jest_failures does); vitest -> the file part of 'FAIL <file> > ...' lines; pytest -> the path before :: on FAILED/ERROR lines; each path kept only when _manifest_phases.is_suite_path accepts it and it lies under no _VENDOR_DIRS segment; a runner whose failure lines name no file (mocha) or an unrecognised runner -> (None, a basis saying which), never an empty list that reads as nothing failed. observed_step sets failingSuites and failingSuitesBasis on a step that exited non-zero and carries no no-verdict outcome: a killed jest worker's FAIL header is not a failing test (jest_worker_signal), so a could-not-run step carries neither. The basis says 'named as failing' only when the paths came off the runner's own failure lines, the wording failing_lines uses, so a learner can refuse anything else. _evidence_io.py: add both keys to STEP_KEYS; bound the list by MAX_PATHS with the cut counted; redact each path through repo_relative_or_token as _paths does; add row_by_run(rows, run_id) beside latest_by_subject (the newest row by ts carrying that runId, or None) as the one lookup the later readers share. Red-first: test_run_test_gate.py feeds real-shaped jest, vitest and pytest failure output and asserts the suite files; a jest run whose only failures are killed workers carries no failingSuites (mutation: drop the outcome guard -> red); allow case: a passing step carries neither key (mutation: set it on every step -> red). test__evidence_io.py: row_for keeps the keys, cuts at MAX_PATHS with a count and tokenises an absolute path outside the project (mutation: skip the redaction -> red); row_by_run returns None for an unknown id and the newest by ts for a repeated one. SECOND OBSERVATION, THE 'suite-running' ANSWER: observed_step records, on EVERY step (passing ones too), suiteReader = the name summary_reader returns for its output (a _SUMMARY_READERS row: jest, vitest, mocha, pytest), or 'none' when it recognises no test runner's summary. A wrapper's line tally (_STEP_WORDS) is not a suite and records 'none'. 'none' is written rather than left absent so that a step recorded BEFORE this field (key absent) stays distinguishable as unknown. It is recorded because a run's text is not kept and measured cannot tell a test suite from a hook list. _evidence_io: suiteReader joins STEP_KEYS; suite_keys(rows) -> {running: step names with any suiteReader other than 'none', silent: names recorded only with 'none', unknown: names recorded only without the field} - the one ledger answer _manifest_phases.phase_gate_suite_gap takes. validate-manifest.py is the caller that holds the manifest path; its 'The one question validate() cannot be asked' block (main validate-manifest.py:118, the index_only_in_bodies precedent) adds the evidence arm. When meta.phaseGate.exclude is non-empty and phase_gate_suite_gap(manifest) returned nothing (so the certain arm has not already fired inside validate()), it calls it again with _evidence_io.suite_keys over the plan's ledger (_evidence_io.project_config_for, read_rows) and prints the warning returned, through the same _warning_groups collapse. An unreadable ledger is said, never read as 'no suite'. Red-first: a jest step records suiteReader jest and a pre-commit-shaped step records 'none' (mutation: derive it from measured -> red on the pre-commit step); suite_keys puts a key seen only in pre-field rows into unknown (mutation: treat absence as 'none' -> red); validate-manifest over a plan whose exclude leaves [lint], with a ledger where lint only ever recorded 'none', prints 'phase gate runs no suite as far as the ledger shows' (allow: a ledger where the left key recorded jest prints nothing).

tasks.title: run-test-gate --own --quiet: the executor's own tests, unrecorded, whole output in a local log
tasks.description: Constraint: executor.runsGate own-tests tells the executor to run the tests task.tests.add names, and today it does that through bare Bash, whose whole output enters its context. The runner's own render is already bounded (_render_steps prints at most _evidence_io.MAX_FAILING failing lines per step) and --quiet already exists (render_quiet), so the fix is a runner path, not a new renderer. Rule: --own requires --task and refuses --record and --reconcile (exit 2, each named). Commands: the task's OWN gate through P71's _manifest_io.gate_entries(phase, task) with source 'task' (a task measured by its phase's gate has nothing of its own), keeping entries that are not meta.buildCommands keys and whose paths (_manifest_phases.gate_entry_paths) all lie among the task's tests.add paths (_manifest_phases.tests_add_path per entry). None left -> exit 2 '<taskId> declares no gate entry pointed at its own tests.add paths (tests.gateBasis=<basis>) - there is nothing of its own to run', which is also what a gate-only task hears. The run goes through run_gate unchanged (bracket, counts, coverage), writes no row and no pointer, and asks no reuse lookup. The whole output of every step goes to <logsDir>/gate-raw/<runId>.log (runId from _evidence_io.new_run_id()), the directory made through the hooks config's ensure_local_dir and logs_dir (reached with _loader.load_hooks_config()), which drops a self-ignoring .gitignore. NOT under the evidence directory: it defaults under the manifest's directory, and ensure_local_dir's own docstring says never to make a self-ignoring directory there. The log is written after run_gate returns, outside the tree bracket, and the render prints 'raw log: <path>' before the verdict. run_gate keeps a step's text only when a caller asks (a keep_text argument), so ordinary runs pay nothing. Red-first (tk1): a fake runner printing far more lines than the bound, through --own --quiet, renders no more than the step lines, MAX_FAILING failing lines per step and the verdict lines, while the log holds every line; mutation: print the step text -> red. Allow cases: --own --record refused; a gate-only task refused with the sentence; the log directory carries the .gitignore marker. Absent logsDir means the config default.
